positiveFlows.title: THE PURPOSE OF THIS AGREEMENT IS TO INVENTORY AND ANALYZE FOREST AND TIMBER PLOT DATA ON NATIONAL FOREST SERVICE LANDS. THE FOREST SERVICE FOREST INVENTORY AND ANALYSIS PROGRAM IS MANDATED TO PROVIDE ACCURATE AND TIMELY INFORMATION ON THE STATUS AND TRENDS OF OUR NATION'S PRIVATE AND PUBLIC FORESTS AND THEIR RESOURCES BASED ON NATIONWIDE INVENTORIES IT DESIGNS AND CONDUCTS WITH PARTNERS ACROSS ALL LANDS, LANDOWNERS, AND WOOD PROCESSING MILLS. THIS DATA AND INFORMATION UNDERLIE VIRTUALLY ALL MAJOR DECISIONS, POLICIES, AND FUTURE OUTLOOKS PERTAINING TO THE FOREST SECTOR. THE FOREST INVENTORY AND ANALYSIS PROGRAM HAS A MISSION OF MAKING AND KEEPING CURRENT A COMPREHENSIVE INVENTORY OF THE NATIONS FORESTS SO THAT POLICY MAKERS, LAND MANAGERS AND OWNERS, INVESTORS, AND OTHER NON-GOVERNMENTAL GROUPS HAVE TIMELY AND ACCURATE INFORMATION ABOUT THE HEALTH AND PRODUCTIVITY OF FORESTS IN THE UNITED STATES.

THE PURPOSE OF THIS AGREEMENT IS TO DOCUMENT THE COOPERATION BETWEEN THE PARTIES TOCOLLECT AND ANALYZE FOREST INVENTORY AND ANALYSIS DATA IN ALASKA WITH PARTICULAR EMPHASIS ON THE INTERIOR ALASKA FOREST INVENTORY AND ANALYSIS UNIT. THIS INCLUDES MAINTAINING PREPAREDNESS OF DOF EMPLOYEES, EQUIPMENT, ANDOPERATIONS, IN ORDER TO EVALUATE FORESTED CONDITIONS IN THE MAINLAND REGION OF ALASKA.

THE PURPOSE OF THIS AGREEMENT IS TO COLLECT TIMBER PRODUCTS OUTPUT (TPO) SURVEY DATA INCLUDING PROCESSING AND ANALYZINGDATA FROM WOOD-USING MILLS SPANNING 24 STATES. THIS TPO CONSISTS OF THREE PARTS. A PRIMARY WOOD USING MILL QUESTIONNAIRE SURVEY, WOOD UTILIZATION FIELD PLOT ANALYSIS, AND FACT SHEET REPORTS AND PUBLISHED DATA ANALYSIS TOOLS FOR INDUSTRY AND STATE AGENCIES TO REFERENCE. THE TPO SURVEY IS A VOLUNTARY SURVEY AIMED AT WOOD USING MILLS AND POWER GENERATING PLANTS TO COLLECT SPECIFIC INFORMATION ABOUT MILL EQUIPMENT, MILL SIZE AND MILL PRODUCTION VOLUME. IT ALSO COMPILES INFORMATION OF ROUNDWOOD SPECIES, ROUNDWOOD VOLUME AND GEOGRAPHICAL LOCATION OF TIMBER HARVESTS FROM WHICH MILLS PROCURE THEIR ROUNDWOOD. TPO IS IMPLEMENTED ON AN ONGOING, ANNUAL BASIS. TPO UTILIZATION PLOTS ARE USED TO GATHER STUMPAGE DATA AND ARE ANALYZED TO DEVELOP VOLUME ESTIMATES OF USABLE WOOD PRODUCTS HARVESTED FROM ESTABLISHED PLOT CATEGORIES ACROSS THE REGION. THE SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS WORK WILL ALLOW FOR BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF UTILIZATION PRACTICES, SPECIES, MARKETS UTILIZATION AND HARVESTED VOLUME OF ROUNDWOOD BY COUNTY. THE COOPERATOR WILL CONDUCT FIELD AND OFFICE WORK TO COMPLETE PROJECT DATA DELIVERABLES.

THIS AGREEMENT SUPPORTS EVALUATION OF THE EFFECTIVENESS OF FUELS AND FOREST MANAGEMENT EFFORTS AT MEETING SPECIFIC MANAGEMENT OBJECTIVES ACROSS NATIONAL FOREST SYSTEM LANDS. OVER THE PAST TWO YEARS, RESEARCH TEAMS FROM THE ROCKY MOUNTAIN RESEARCH STATION AND PACIFIC SOUTHWEST RESEARCH STATION HAVE DEVELOPED A SET OF METRICS THAT MEASURE THE OUTCOMES OF FUELS AND FOREST MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES AND OTHER VEGETATION TREATMENTS AND DISTURBANCES WITH RESPECT TO WILDFIRE RISK AND LANDSCAPE CONDITIONS. THESE METRICS WERE DEVELOPED AND TESTED ON 21 HIGH-RISK LANDSCAPES IN THE WESTERN UNITED STATES. WORK UNDER THIS AGREEMENT WILL APPLY THE OUTCOME CONDITION METRICS TO HIGH VALUE LANDSCAPES ACROSS THE NATION TO ASSESS THE VALUE AND IMPACT OF INVESTMENTS IN FUEL REDUCTION ON WILDFIRE RISK REDUCTION AND FOREST HEALTH.

THE SURVEY IS CONDUCTED BY CONTACTING APPROXIMATELY 15,000 PRIVATE LANDOWNERS EACH YEAR AND ASKING THEM TO COMPLETE A SELF-ADMINISTERED MAIL SURVEY. THE WORK WILL PRODUCE A COMPREHENSIVE SET OF PRODUCTS THAT IDENTIFY REACH-SCALE FLOODPLAIN RESTORATION POTENTIAL RELATED TO WATER QUALITY RESILIENCE TO WILDFIRE. RESULTS WILL BE SHARED THROUGH PUBLICATIONS AND PRESENTATIONS TO SUPPORT FOREST MANAGERS, WILDFIRE PLANNING, RESTORATION PRACTITIONERS, LOCAL COMMUNITY WATER SUPPLY MANAGERS, AND LANDSCAPE-SCALE PLANNERS. IF THIS AWARD IS NOT APPROVED, THE FOREST SERVICE AND PARTNERS WILL HAVE LITTLE GUIDANCE IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF REGIONALLY AND LOCALLY INFORMED FLOODPLAIN RESTORATION PROJECTS THAT ARE DESIGNED WITH THE GOAL OF REDUCING WATER QUALITY IMPAIRMENT FOLLOWING WILDFIRE. WITHOUT THIS WORK, FOREST MANAGERS AND MUNICIPAL WATER SUPPLIERS WILL LACK PRACTICAL, SCIENCE-BASED GUIDANCE TO SITE FLOODPLAIN RECONNECTION PROJECTS, REDUCING EFFICACY OF UPSLOPE WILDFIRE SEVERITY TREATMENTS AND MAKING WATERSHEDS LESS RESILIENT TO WILDFIRE. THIS HAS THE POTENTIAL TO AFFECT LONG-TERM FOREST PRODUCTIVITY AND HUMAN COMMUNITY RECOVERY TO WILDFIRE.

THIS PROJECT INVOLVES TRAINING EMERGING PROFESSIONALS INTERNSHIP CORPS MEMBERS TO TAKE FIELD MEASUREMENTS OF IMPORTANT FOREST COMPONENTS THAT INCLUDE TREES, SHRUBS, WEEDS, DOWNED WOODY DEBRIS, AND WILDLIFE. THE PROJECTS ARE IN OREGON, WASHINGTON, AND CALIFORNIA. THE INFORMATION COLLECTED WILL BE USED TO ACCELERATE MANAGEMENT ACTIONS OUTLINED IN PRESIDENTIAL AND ADMINISTRATION PRIORITIES AROUND TIMBER PRODUCTION, REDUCING FIRE FUEL LOADS, CONTROLLING INVASIVE SPECIES, AND REDUCING LITIGATION AROUND FOREST MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES. THE LEARNING ACTIVITIES CONDUCTED BY MEMBERS WILL HELP FOSTER THE NEXT GENERATION OF NATURAL RESOURCE PROFESSIONALS FOR THE AGENCY. FAILURE TO APPROVE THIS AGREEMENT WILL RESULT IN SUBSTANTIAL DELAY (ONE OR MORE YEARS) OF TIMBER HARVESTING AND REDUCING FIRE FUEL LOAD ON SEVERAL PROJECTS AT SEVERAL NATIONAL FORESTS IN THE PACIFIC NORTHWEST. THEREFORE, IT WOULD PUT AT RISK OUR ABILITY TO MEET CURRENT ADMINISTRATIVE PRIORITIES FOR TIMBER PRODUCTION AND FIRE FUEL LOAD REDUCTION. FURTHER, THERE WILL BE INSUFFICIENT DATA COLLECTED TO INFORM POST-FIRE MANAGEMENT DECISIONS, INCLUDING CONTROL OF NOXIOUS WEEDS, TREE REGENERATION, AND POST-FIRE TIMBER HARVEST. THIS INFORMATION IS NEEDED TO ENSURE FUTURE TIMBER PRODUCTION.

THIS PROJECT SUPPORTS RESEARCH ON THE EFFECTS OF THINNING AND PRESCRIBED BURNING TREATMENTS ON IMPROVING FOREST HEALTH AND INCREASING RESILIENCE TO WILDFIRE. WORK WILL OCCUR AT EXISTING AND NEWLY ESTABLISHED STUDY SITES IN HIGH-ELEVATION AND LOWER-ELEVATION DRY CONIFER FORESTS THAT HAVE EXPERIENCED HARVEST, PRESCRIBED FIRE, OR WILDFIRE. FIELD ACTIVITIES INCLUDE COLLECTING DATA ON TREE CHARACTERISTICS, TREE SURVIVAL, FIRE-CAUSED INJURY, BARK BEETLE ATTACK, BLISTER RUST PREVALENCE, AND FUEL LOADING TO EVALUATE HOW TREATMENTS AND WILDFIRE AFFECT FOREST STRUCTURE, COMPOSITION, AND LONG-TERM ECOSYSTEM RESPONSES. THE EFFORT INCLUDES DEVELOPING PUBLICATIONS AND TECHNOLOGY-TRANSFER MATERIALS TO INFORM LAND MANAGERS ON NATIONAL FORESTS, PRIVATE LAND MANAGERS AND FORESTRY RESEARCHERS. THIS RESEARCH DIRECTLY SUPPORTS PRIORITIES OF THE FOREST SERVICE (FS), INCLUDING ACTIVE MANAGEMENT FOR FOREST HEALTH AND PRODUCTIVITY, STRENGTHENED PARTNERSHIPS THAT PRODUCE ON-THE-GROUND OUTCOMES, AND PROTECTION OF COMMUNITIES AND NATURAL RESOURCES FROM WILDFIRE. THE PROJECT WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED THROUGH COORDINATED FIELD DATA COLLECTION, ANALYSIS, AND SYNTHESIS. RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE DOCUMENTING TREATMENT AND WILDFIRE EFFECTS; COLLECTING, STORING, AND MANAGING DATA AND PRODUCING MANUSCRIPTS AND GUIDANCE DOCUMENTS IN COLLABORATION WITH THE FS. THE FS WILL PROVIDE PROTOCOLS, SAMPLING EQUIPMENT, COMPUTERS, SAFETY AND TECHNICAL TRAINING, AND GUIDANCE ON INFORMATION SYNTHESIS AND PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT. RESULTS WILL BE SHARED AT SCIENTIFIC CONFERENCES SUCH AS THE INTERNATIONAL FIRE ECOLOGY AND MANAGEMENT CONGRESS AND THE WHITEBARK PINE SCIENCE AND MANAGEMENT CONFERENCE. THE WORK CONTRIBUTES TO LONG-TERM RESEARCH, SUPPORTS DEVELOPMENT OF PEER-REVIEWED PUBLICATIONS, AND PROVIDES MANAGERSSUCH AS SILVICULTURISTS, FUELS SPECIALISTS, AND PLANNING STAFFWITH INFORMATION NEEDED TO DESIGN, IMPLEMENT, AND EVALUATE THINNING AND BURNING TREATMENTS CONSISTENT WITH FS PRIORITIES.
